---
title: "Technical details"
---

quartodown builds the site in three stages: it generates a
[Quarto](https://quarto.org/) website project from the package sources, renders
it with Quarto, and adds hover tooltips to the result. The man pages, vignettes
and the [pkgdown](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/)-style layout around them are all
Quarto pages, so every Quarto feature works.

## How a build works

`quartodown::build_site()` runs in three stages:

1. **Before rendering**, it writes a Quarto project into `_quarto/`: a reference
   page per man page, the vignettes, the changelog, license and community files,
   and the generated pages and theme files below.
2. **During rendering**, Quarto renders `_quarto/` into `docs/`, running the
   examples and vignette code. Quarto runs each page's code in a new R process,
   which loads the package from the library, so `build_site()` first installs
   the package into a temporary library and puts it first on that process's
   library path. With `build_site(devel = TRUE)`, it skips the install and has
   each process load the package from source with `pkgload::load_all()`.
3. **After rendering**, it adds hover tooltips to the HTML in `docs/`.

The only file you edit is `_quartodown.yml`. Everything in `_quarto/` is
rewritten on every build, and gitignored by `quartodown::use_quartodown()`:

```text
_quarto/
├── _quarto.yml                   # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.md                      # home page
├── reference/
│   ├── index.qmd                 # function reference index
│   └── <topic>.qmd               # a page per man/*.Rd
├── authors.qmd                   # authors and citation page
├── vignettes/                    # the vignettes, as they are
├── man/figures/                  # images for the README and man pages
├── NEWS.md                       # changelog, with issues and users linked
├── quartodown.scss               # pkgdown-style theme on top of Quarto's HTML
├── quartodown-header.html        # dark-mode default
└── quartodown-after-body.html    # navbar alignment
```

As in pkgdown, the reference pages are served at `reference/<topic>.html`, and
`docs/pkgdown.yml` tells other sites' [downlit](https://downlit.r-lib.org/)
links where to find them.

## Before rendering

### The home page

`index.md` holds the README next to a pkgdown-style sidebar with links, the
license, the citation, the developers and the README's badges. On narrow screens
the sidebar moves below the content.

A README `<picture>` with a light and a dark version (GitHub's
`prefers-color-scheme` convention) becomes one `<img>` per theme, switched by
the site's light/dark toggle.

### The reference index

To group and order the function index, `_quartodown.yml` has a `reference:`
field in the same shape as pkgdown's:

```yaml
reference:
  - title: Building the site       # <1>
    desc: >                        # <2>
      Set up a package, then build its site.
    contents:
      - use_quartodown                # <3>
      - starts_with("build_")      # <4>
```

1. Each entry becomes a section of the index, with this heading.
2. An optional description, shown under the heading.
3. A topic, by any of its `\alias{}` names.
4. A selector, as in pkgdown: `starts_with()`, `ends_with()`, `contains()`,
   `matches()`, `has_concept()`, `has_keyword()`, `-` to exclude and `c()` to
   combine.

### The navbar and footer

The navbar links the "Get started" vignette, the reference index, the other
vignettes under "Articles" and the changelog. The footer has pkgdown's
"Developed by ..." text, built from `Authors@R`.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Changing the Quarto configuration

A `quarto:` field in `quartodown.yml` is merged over the generated
configuration. Lists, like the navbar's items, are appended to; any other
setting is replaced, and `~` removes it. For example, to add a navbar link and
fold code blocks:

```yaml
quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com
  format:
    html:
      code-fold: true
```
:::

## The man pages

Each `man/*.Rd` file, except `\keyword{internal}` ones, becomes
`_quarto/reference/<name>.qmd`. It's rendered to HTML with `tools::Rd2HTML()`,
as R's help does, and then adjusted to look like pkgdown's:

- **Rd macros** work: the package's own (`RdMacros:` in `DESCRIPTION`, or
  `man/macros/`), such as Rdpack's `\insertRef{}`, and build-time `\Sexpr{}`s
  such as `\doi{}`.
- **Usage**, and code blocks with a language, such as roxygen's
  ```` ```yaml ````, are syntax-highlighted with a copy button.
- **Inline code** is rendered as Markdown code spans, so quotes and backslashes
  survive Pandoc, and `\eqn{}`/`\deqn{}` render as math.
- **Examples** run, with their output in the same block, prefixed with `#>`.
  `\dontrun{}` code is shown but not run, `\dontshow{}` code is run but not
  shown, and `@examplesIf` examples run only if their condition holds. A page
  whose examples all are in `\dontrun{}` renders without starting an R session.

## After rendering: hover tooltips

After rendering, `build_site()` links every reference to one of the package's
functions, in code blocks or inline code, to its man page. Hovering shows a
tooltip with its usage and the first sentence of its description. Try it: hover
over `build_site()` or `use_quartodown()`.

The sentence is cut off at 200 characters, and `build_site()` warns when one is
longer. To build without tooltips, use `build_site(tooltips = FALSE)`.

## Matching the pkgdown look

`quartodown.scss` is styled after pkgdown's `pkgdown.scss`, written for Quarto's
HTML, and layered on top of Quarto's own themes:

```yaml
theme:
  light: [default, quartodown.scss]
  dark: [darkly, quartodown.scss]
```

`darkly` normally uses the Lato web font and larger headings, so text would
reflow when toggling between light and dark. `quartodown.scss` therefore sets
Bootstrap's system font stack and heading sizes for both themes.

Two things need JavaScript:

- **Dark mode by default.** `quartodown-header.html` starts new visitors on the
  dark theme if their system prefers it.
- **Aligning the navbar title with the body text.** The body's left edge differs
  between the home page and other pages, so `quartodown-after-body.html`
  measures it and adjusts the navbar's padding.
